lines.text: The British car market offers a bewildering array of vehicle types, each designed for different needs and lifestyles. The hatchback remains Britain's most popular body style — compact, practical, and affordable, with a rear door that opens upward to access the boot. The Ford Fiesta (until its discontinuation in 2023) and Volkswagen Golf have been perennial bestsellers. Saloons (called 'sedans' in American English) offer a separate enclosed boot and a more formal appearance — the BMW 3 Series and Mercedes C-Class dominate this segment. Estate cars extend the roofline to the rear, creating a larger boot space — ideal for families, dog owners, and those who value practicality over style. SUVs (Sport Utility Vehicles) have surged in popularity, now accounting for nearly half of all new car sales in Britain. Their higher driving position, larger interior, and robust appearance appeal to buyers, though critics question their fuel consumption and urban suitability. Crossovers blur the line between SUV and hatchback — raised ride height with car-like handling. MPVs (Multi-Purpose Vehicles), once popular for large families, have largely been displaced by SUVs. Electric vehicles (EVs) are transforming the market: the UK government has set a 2035 ban on new petrol and diesel car sales, pushing manufacturers to electrify their ranges. Hybrid vehicles — combining petrol engines with electric motors — serve as a transitional technology.
